newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Mozambique sign oil refinery memorandum.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Mozambique sign oil refinery memorandum.

text.p: Iran and Mozambique on Thursday signed an agreement on building an oil refinery in the African country, state-run Tehran radio said.

It said Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh and Mozambican Mineral Resources and Energy Minister John Kachamila signed a memorandum of understanding in Tehran under which Iran agreed to provide technical know-how and supply crude oil.

Aghazadeh said the refinery would have to be funded by several southern African states and other foreign investors and that "Iran is ready to cooperate with Mozambique in this respect." He did not elaborate.
Under the memorandum, Mozambique committed itself to provide the "desired conditions" for the refinery's construction, the radio added without elaborating.
Iranian officials have said Tehran wanted to help set up a refinery in the northern Mozambican port city of Nacala and to rebuild the country's existing refinery at Matola in the south.

Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway. Tehran plans to open soon its eighth refinery in Bandar Abbas near the mouth of the Gulf, which officials say has been designed and built by Iranian exports.
